jobs.prompt: TOP PRIORITY, field report from the atlas project (the hand-build guard refused plain swarm handbuild status six times with the approve-or-deny message). Findings: the project hook in .claude/settings.local.json (and settings.json) points at <install base>/tools/handbuild-guard.mjs, NOT <install base>/current/tools/handbuild-guard.mjs, dated a day old, and it loads sibling modules of an older release. Cause in tools/install.mjs: stableInstallDir(installRoot) only maps to the current folder when the install root sits under a versions folder; when update was run from the base folder itself it returns the base, so the hook is pinned to whatever tools folder happened to be the install root. Also in bumpPointers (tools/swarm/core-12.mjs) a pinned project is skipped (continue) BEFORE its hooks are refreshed, so a pinned project never gets a corrected guard. Fix: (1) stableInstallDir(installRoot): resolve symlinks; if the path is under a versions folder map to the sibling current as today; else if installRoot/current exists as a directory or symlink that contains tools/swarm.mjs, use installRoot/current; otherwise keep installRoot. A hook command is always built from this result, for every hook script (guard, orchestrator hook, checkpoint). (2) Refresh: every swarm update (updateProjects and bumpPointers), swarm handbuild install, swarm init and swarm doctor if it exists rewrite any hook whose command path differs from the stable path, in BOTH .claude/settings.local.json and .claude/settings.json (read settings.json; update only entries whose command contains one of our script names, keep everything else byte-for-byte apart from our command strings; never create settings.json when missing; a tracked settings.json that gets changed is reported as hooks-path-fixed-tracked so the owner can commit it, but nothing is committed). (3) Move the hook refresh in bumpPointers so it runs for pinned projects too (the guard is a safety control; the pin only stops the version pointer move, and the hook points at current anyway); a pinned project is reported as hooks refreshed, pointer skipped. (4) Add a self-check in the hook command itself or a swarm handbuild status line: status prints the guard hook path in use and whether it equals the stable path, and warns when a hook points at a path that is not under current. (5) The approve matcher: confirm in tools/self-approval.mjs, tools/shell-writes.mjs and tools/handbuild.mjs that the owner-verb test looks only at the subcommand position (after swarm, the optional --root value, the word handbuild; or the decide subcommand with a handbuild id) and never at the words of --reason, --files, other flag values, quoted strings, heredocs, comments or earlier commands joined with && ; | ;. Add a regression test with reasons containing approve, approved, approving, deny, denied, on, off, and swarm handbuild approve inside quotes, in single and double quotes and after echo, for the verbs request, status, list, show, log: all allowed; and the real approve forms still blocked, including after a && and after env prefixes. Tests in tests/hook-path-stable.test.mjs and tests/handbuild-reason-words.test.mjs, hermetic (temp install base with versions and current symlink, temp project, no ambient environment, no network): the install base without versions but with current yields the current path; versions layout unchanged; no current keeps the base; update rewrites a stale base-path hook in settings.local.json and in a tracked settings.json (other entries untouched byte for byte, no file created when missing, nothing staged or committed); a pinned project gets hooks refreshed and pointer untouched; handbuild status prints the hook path and warns on a stale one; the reason-word matrix above through guardDecision and through the hook script on stdin. Keep every existing test passing (install, hooks, pins, handbuild guard, orchestrator hook tests). Never import install.mjs statically from new modules. Tests are hermetic. No token-shaped literals. ignoreTests reason: only the named files and their tests change.
